Article Title: Apple launches new Health AI study app to understand how people use AI for medical advice
Article Text:
The Apple Health AI Usage Study aims to inform the responsible design of health AI experiences by examining what drives user trust, the quality of responses, comprehension, and everyday health actions. (Image: Apple)

Dedicated app allows users to ask health questions

Apple targets up to 200,000 participants

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Privacy and safeguards

Apple has launched the new Apple Health AI Usage Study in the United States. It is a virtual research study and associated app which is designed to advance the understanding of how people interact with conversational health AI tools. “At Apple, we believe responsible innovation starts with scientific rigor and clinical grounding. Health is deeply personal, and conducting a dedicated research study is the most thoughtful way to understand how people engage with, comprehend, and evaluate health AI in everyday life,” said Sumbul Desai, M.D., Apple’s vice president of Health and Fitness. “Insights from this study will help advance the broader scientific conversation and ensure that as technology evolves, we continue building trusted tools that genuinely support people wherever they are on their health journey.”As part of the initiative, Apple has released a dedicated iOS app that lets participants ask health-related questions and receive responses grounded in clinical research. Answers are supported by peer-reviewed medical sources, including publications such as The New England Journal of Medicine, JAMA and Nature, according to Apple and OpenEvidence. Users can rate responses and provide feedback on factors such as relevance, detail and usefulness.Participants will also be asked to complete regular surveys to help researchers better understand how AI-generated health information is interpreted and used.Apple is planning to enrol around 2,00,000 adults in the United States for the virtual study. The eligible participants must be at least 21 years old and use an iPhone 15-series device or later running iOS 26 or above. The participants can optionally share the HealthKit data information such as activity, sleep, heart rate and lab results enabling the app to create more personalised responses.The tech giant said that the data will be anonymised before being sent to a secure third-party cloud provider and will not be used to train AI models. OpenEvidence will delete query and response data after 24 hours, according to the company.Apple says the study was designed with privacy protections, transparency and clinical guardrails. Study data won’t be used to train AI models, and participants control whether to share HealthKit metrics or survey responses. The app has safety guardrails meant to detect certain concerning questions and suggest following up with a provider or other resources. Apple stresses that the app isn’t meant to diagnose or treat any condition or replace a medical professional’s advice.
Article Summary: Apple has launched the new Apple Health AI Usage Study in the United States. It is a virtual research study and associated app which is designed to advance the understanding of how people interact with conversational health AI tools. Apple is planning to enrol around 2,00,000 adults in the U.S for the virtual study.

Article Title: Samsung highlights AI-powered washing machine for winter laundry needs
Article Text:
AI Wash adjusts settings automatically

Auto Dispense and AI Control simplify operation

Faster washing with QuickDrive and Super Speed

Focus on hygiene and large-capacity washing

Smart home connectivity and after-sales support

Samsung has spotlighted its WW12DB8B54GBTL AI-powered washing machine, positioning it as a solution for households managing winter clothing and bulky fabrics. The company said the appliance combines artificial intelligence features, automated detergent dispensing and connected home capabilities to simplify laundry routines. In a statement, Samsung said winter garments such as sweaters, jackets, blankets and bedsheets often require different wash settings, making laundry management more complex. The company claims its AI-powered technologies can automatically optimise washing parameters based on the type and condition of each load.One of the key features of the WW12DB8B54GBTL is AI Wash, which uses sensors to analyse load weight, fabric softness and soiling levels. Based on this information, the machine automatically adjusts water usage, detergent levels, soaking duration, rinsing and spinning cycles. Samsung said the technology can reduce detergent consumption by up to 15% while delivering tailored washing performance for different fabric types.The machine also comes with an Auto Dispense system that automatically releases the required amount of detergent and fabric softener for each wash cycle, eliminating the need for manual measurement.Meanwhile, AI Control is designed to learn users' washing habits over time and recommend frequently used programmes, helping streamline day-to-day use.Samsung has equipped the appliance with QuickDrive and Super Speed technologies targeted at users who need quicker washing cycles. According to the company, QuickDrive can reduce washing time by up to 57.5%, while the Super Speed mode can complete a wash cycle in as little as 39 minutes under specified conditions.The WW12DB8B54GBTL also features AI Ecobubble technology, which creates detergent bubbles designed to improve cleaning performance, and Hygiene Steam for deeper cleaning through steam-based wash cycles. Despite a 600mm-wide body, the machine offers a 12kg washing capacity through Samsung's SpaceMax design, making it suitable for larger households and bulky items such as comforters and blankets.The washing machine supports Samsung's SmartThings platform, allowing users to connect and manage the appliance through the company's smart home ecosystem.Samsung said the model is powered by a Digital Inverter Motor backed by a 10-year warranty. The company added that it supports customers through more than 3,000 service touchpoints and 12,500 trained engineers across India.Samsung described the WW12DB8B54GBTL as a combination of AI-driven convenience, durability and energy-efficient performance, aimed at consumers seeking a more automated laundry experience.
Article Summary: Samsung's WW12DB8B54GBTL machine is aimed at households managing winter clothing and bulky fabrics. The appliance combines artificial intelligence features, automated detergent dispensing and connected home capabilities to simplify laundry routines. Samsung claims its AI-powered technologies can automatically optimise washing parameters based on the type and condition of each load.

Article Title: Days after DoorDash, Uber said their customers hardly use AI Agents and Amazon banned Meta Muse; OpenAI remains ‘unbothered’, launches ChatGPT's new Wallet
Article Text:
Days after DoorDash, Uber said their customers hardly use AI Agents and Amazon banned Meta Muse; OpenAI remains ‘unbothered’, launches ChatGPT's new Wallet

OpenAI launched ChatGPT Wallet: How it will work

Amazon bans Meta Muse over ‘safety concerns’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Sam Altman-led OpenAI has launched ChatGPT Wallet that lets agents pay without access to users’ actual card details. Built in partnership with American Express, Mastercard, and Visa, ChatGPT Wallet will initially be available through dots⁠ for ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the US. In its official announcement, OpenAI said that “with ChatGPT Wallet, we’re now helping people complete purchase, and giving their agents a way to pay that businesses can accept with their existing systems. The announcement comes after Amazon banned Meta Muse and other AI agents from shopping on its platform. Similarly, Uber, DoorDash and Airbnb said that AI agents aren't ‘taking off’.With the ChatGPT Wallet, users can add a card once. They can then approve each purchase without re-entering their payment details. Before each purchase, the user reviews the items, total, and selected card, then approves it with a security check such as Face ID or a fingerprint scan.After the user approves, the payment network provides a payment token—a substitute for the user’s actual card details—with a card number, security code, and expiration date. The payment will then be charged to their selected card without ChatGPT Wallet sharing their actual card details with the business or agent.The company says that to accept payment from ChatGPT Wallet, websites need to ensure agents are not inadvertently blocked, and payment and risk systems need to recognize legitimate purchases made by agents.Earlier this month, Amazon blocked Meta's new AI shopping agent, Muse, from buying on its site. Announcing the ban, Amazon CEO Andy Jassy said outside shopping bots are not yet worth worrying about. Speaking on the company's earnings call, Andy Jassy said few customers are shopping through outside agents because the experience is still not great and no more convenient than ordering directly from a retailer.The remarks come about a month after Amazon cut off Muse, which Meta rolled out in early September. Users trying to place orders through the agent began seeing an error saying that access by an unauthorised AI agent violates Amazon's Conditions of Use. Amazon cited safety concerns. While Jassy did not name Muse, but the timing made the target clear.Similarly, Uber and DoorDash recently said at their latest earnings calls that they've received hundreds of orders through AI agents like Meta's Muse or Instinct. "It is very, very early, and very limited traction that we have seen so far," Uber CFO Balaji Krishnamurthy said. Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky also revealed that only a negligible portion of bookings on the app are made using AI agents.
Article Summary: ChatGPT Wallet lets agents pay without access to users’ actual card details. Built in partnership with American Express, Mastercard, and Visa. Will initially be available through dots⁠ for ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the US. Comes after Amazon banned Meta Muse and other AI agents from shopping on its platform.

Article Title: A 200-year-old roof tile found at a UK salvage yard carries a handwritten dismissal message to a worker named John Lewis, possibly linking it to an 1820 Staffordshire brickmaking business
Article Text:
PC: AI Generated

A 200-year-old dismissal message found on a Staffordshire roof tile

What does the inscription on the old tile reveal about its history

What makes this historic roofing tile an unusual discovery

Why the salvage company wants to preserve its unusual discoveries

A handwritten message believed to be about 200 years old has been discovered on a Staffordshire Blue roof tile at a salvage yard in Rugeley, Staffordshire. The inscription appears to record the dismissal of a worker named John Lewis by someone called Thomas Austin. It was written into soft clay before the tile was fired, preserving the words through about two centuries of use on a roof.According to the BBC, the tile was found at Cawarden Reclaim, where staff recognised its possible historical importance. Research identified a business called Thomas Austin Brick & Tile Makers at Clay Hills, Stoke-on-Trent, in 1820.The inscription was found on a Staffordshire Blue roof tile at Cawarden Reclaim, a salvage yard in Rugeley. It reads, “I do hereby discharge you, John Lewis, from my employment, Thomas Austin.” The message appears to be a written notice that Lewis was no longer employed.The words had been written into soft clay before the tile was fired, leaving them preserved on the finished roofing material. The yard describes the tile as about 200 years old.General manager Adam Giles said, "We were looking around and we just happened to come across this tile.”He took it back to the yard, cleaned it, and quickly felt it had historical significance. The company said the name, location, and period made a potential connection, based on its research into a business identified in 1820.The company conceded it did not know for certain that the two were linked. The company had found a firm called Thomas Austin Brick & Tile Makers, based at Clay Hills, Stoke-on-Trent, in 1820. Giles said, "If it is the same person [Thomas Austin], we may have uncovered not only a glimpse into somebody's working life in the early 19th century, but also a connection to the people who made the very building materials that have survived to this day. "Giles said, "You come across quite a few pawprints from animals and old shoes, where they used to walk across the clay while they were being fired.”However, he said handwritten text on a tile was much less common. He described the discovery as very unusual and rare. The inscription was made before the clay was fired, and the finished tile was later used for its intended purpose as roofing material.Giles said, "The fact that someone went to the trouble of writing that out on the back of clay before it was fired, and then firing the tile and using it for the purpose it was designed for.”Cawarden Reclaim said it found intriguing items such as this from time to time. When staff found items considered noteworthy, they kept them aside and preserved them. The company said these objects would eventually be displayed in its reception area as part of a wall of interest. The tile’s inscription appears to record a direct message from an employer to a named worker, but the circumstances behind the dismissal are not known from the discovery. Nor has the company confirmed that the Thomas Austin named in the message was linked to the Stoke-on-Trent brick and tile business.
Article Summary: Inscription was found on a Staffordshire Blue roof tile at Cawarden Reclaim, a salvage yard in Rugeley. It reads, “I do hereby discharge you, John Lewis, from my employment, Thomas Austin.” The tile’s inscription appears to record a direct message from an employer to a named worker.

Article Title: A British collector bought an 1834 silver coin for just £8 at a car boot sale; 3D scans have now uncovered evidence of a possible minting accident hidden for 192 years
Article Text:
3D scans reveal unusual patterns of damage

Why researchers suspect a minting accident

A rare survivor from the steam-powered minting era

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A badly damaged silver coin dating back to 1834 may hold clues to an unusual manufacturing accident that occurred nearly two centuries ago. What initially appeared to be an ordinary damaged antique has now become the subject of a scientific investigation, with researchers suggesting that the coin may have been crushed during the original minting process. According to a report published by ScienceDaily on November 11, 2026, the findings are based on a study by IA STUDIO published in the journal npj Heritage Science. Independent coverage by EurekAlert and Science News has also highlighted the unusual physical evidence uncovered during the investigation. The coin, a silver sixpence issued during the reign of King William IV, was discovered in an album containing assorted coins at a car boot sale in Greater Manchester, England. It had been individually marked with a price tag of £8, although the album was eventually purchased as a single lot rather than the sixpence being sold separately. What makes the discovery particularly interesting is the coin’s unusual condition. Its central sections are severely distorted, with much of the original design barely recognisable. However, parts of its outer rim and the grooves along its edge remain surprisingly intact.This contrast prompted researchers to investigate whether the damage had occurred through years of circulation, corrosion, an accidental impact or something that went wrong during manufacturing.To understand the coin’s condition, researchers combined scanning electron microscopy, chemical analysis and optical surface profilometry, a technique used to create detailed three-dimensional maps of an object’s surface. The scans revealed deep depressions, raised ridges and overlapping layers of displaced metal. The damage was particularly pronounced on the front of the coin, known as the obverse, which carries the portrait of William IV.Measurements showed a height difference of approximately 0.75 millimetres across the damaged central portrait area. Although this may seem insignificant, it represents substantial deformation on the surface of a thin silver coin. The distribution of the damage proved especially important. Rather than showing the gradual smoothing typically associated with years of handling, the coin displayed sharp depressions and distinct raised sections, suggesting that considerable force had been applied to specific areas. Researchers believe the pattern is most consistent with repeated applications of intense pressure, with the metal’s ability to spread sideways appearing to have been restricted.Chemical examinations provided further information about the coin’s composition. Less damaged sections contained a silver and copper alloy, while the distorted areas showed changes associated with corrosion and surface contamination.However, these chemical changes could not explain the depth and arrangement of the physical damage. The three-dimensional measurements offered stronger evidence that the metal had undergone substantial mechanical deformation.The researchers therefore considered several possible explanations, including ordinary wear, corrosion, accidental damage after production and compression under restricted conditions. Their findings favoured an unusual striking anomaly during the original manufacturing process. However, the study does not establish the precise sequence of events or rule out every possibility of later damage.The sixpence was produced in 1834, when Britain was already using steam-powered presses to manufacture coins. Mechanised production allowed mints to strike coins on a much larger scale, but manufacturing defects could still occur. Severely defective coins were generally identified during quality inspections and melted down so that their precious metal could be reused. This makes the survival of an unusually damaged silver coin particularly interesting to researchers.If the proposed explanation is correct, the sixpence could offer a rare physical record of a manufacturing failure from the early period of mechanised British coin production. The investigation also explored the use of artificial intelligence in historical research. Computational tools helped the study’s author, A. Ikraam of IA STUDIO, organise observations, consider competing explanations and formulate questions for laboratory testing. However, the conclusions were based on independently obtained scientific measurements rather than AI-generated findings.The laboratory work involved the Experimental Techniques Centre at Brunel University of London and the Oxford Materials Characterisation Service at the University of Oxford. The research demonstrates how modern imaging and materials analysis can reveal details that might otherwise remain hidden in historical objects. For a coin that spent nearly two centuries with its origins of damage unexplained, its distorted surface may now offer an unusual glimpse into the workings of Britain’s 19th-century mints.
Article Summary: The silver sixpence was discovered in an album containing assorted coins at a car boot sale in Greater Manchester, England. Its central sections are severely distorted, with much of the original design barely recognisable. But parts of its outer rim and the grooves along its edge remain surprisingly intact. Researchers suggest the coin may have been crushed during the original minting process.

Article Title: Meet Chris Qian, the Virginia teen who started ReTech for Kids at 14, helped distribute 2,000 refurbished devices with over 100 youth volunteers, won a $5,000 pitch prize and earned a 2026 Diana Award
Article Text:

The problem he saw

How the nonprofit works

The impact so far

Recognition from UVM

The Diana Award

Why the work matters

What comes next

Chris Qian was only 14 when he founded ReTech for Kids, a nonprofit that collects, refurbishes, and redistributes second-hand technology to under-resourced students across the United States. Three years later, the initiative has mobilised more than 100 youth volunteers, helped distribute 2,000 refurbished devices, and earned Qian a $5,000 prize at the University of Vermont’s 2026 Vermont Pitch Challenge, according to the Diana Award Roll of Honour, UVM, and MIT Solve.Qian’s work began with a simple observation: many students do not have reliable access to a personal computer, while usable devices are often discarded or left unused. Rather than treating that as an unavoidable reality, he built a system that turns unwanted electronics into practical learning tools for young people who need them most. Read more about his work, as per the reports, here:ReTech for Kids was created to address the digital divide, a gap that affects students who lack reliable access to devices, internet, or the skills needed to use them. According to the organisation’s MIT Solve profile, UNICEF estimates that about 1.3 billion children ages 3 to 18 worldwide do not have reliable access to personal devices.That gap has consequences beyond homework. Students without their own computer may struggle to attend virtual classes, complete assignments, learn coding, or explore interests such as video editing that require capable hardware.Qian’s solution is to give those students fully functioning devices rather than asking them to buy new ones.For many recipients, the donated computer is their first personal computer, which makes the difference even more significant.ReTech for Kids collects devices through partnerships with businesses and community centres. Student volunteers then diagnose, repair, and upgrade each device, replacing hard drives with SSDs, increasing RAM, cleaning internal components, and testing keyboards, batteries, and displays.The organisation also uses lightweight Linux distributions to make older devices usable, since they can run well on hardware that may no longer support Windows or macOS. Qian is developing a modified version of Linux Mint XFCE called ReTechOS, designed specifically for students and first-time computer owners.Once a device passes quality checks, ReTech for Kids partners with other nonprofits to identify students most in need. Devices are delivered with basic digital literacy guides and, where possible, access to ongoing technical support.Over three years, Qian has led more than 100 youth volunteers and helped distribute 2,000 refurbished devices. The Diana Award Roll of Honour describes the initiative as combining environmental responsibility with educational opportunity, since it diverts unwanted electronics away from landfills while putting them into the hands of students.That dual benefit is part of what makes the model compelling. A laptop that might otherwise be thrown away becomes a tool for learning, and a student who might otherwise be excluded from digital opportunities gains a way to participate.The work has also given young volunteers a role in the process. They are not just recipients of a service, they are the people collecting, repairing, and distributing the devices, which builds both technical skills and a sense of ownership.Qian’s work earned second place in the 2026 Vermont Pitch Challenge, a Shark Tank-like competition for high school entrepreneurs. He received a $5,000 prize for ReTech for Kids, which was described by UVM as a nonprofit that refurbishes and donates laptops and other devices to K-12 students to close the digital divide and reduce e-waste.The competition drew more than 100 teams from 24 U.S. states, with five finalist teams invited to pitch in person at UVM on April 7, 2026. Qian’s placement among that group reflects both the strength of the idea and the clarity with which he presented it.The prize money is not just a reward. It is also a signal that the work is being taken seriously by judges, educators, and entrepreneurs who see the value in a student-led solution to a real-world problem.In 2026, Qian was also named a recipient of the Diana Award, an honour that recognises young people for their social action and humanitarian work. The Roll of Honour describes him as someone who has demonstrated the ability to inspire and mobilise others to create long-lasting change.The award highlights Qian’s ability to combine practical action with a broader vision. He is not only distributing devices, he is building a model that others can replicate, using volunteers, partnerships, and refurbished technology to address a persistent inequality.At 17, Qian is already being recognised alongside young leaders from around the world. That recognition reflects the scale of what he has built, even though the organisation began with a single student’s concern about access to technology.The digital divide is not just a technology issue, it is an education and opportunity issue. Students who lack access to devices may fall behind in school, miss out on digital skills, and face barriers when they enter the workforce.ReTech for Kids addresses that problem at its source. By refurbishing and redistributing devices, Qian is creating a practical, scalable way to put technology into the hands of students who need it most.The initiative also shows how young people can lead on issues that adults often struggle to solve. Qian saw a gap, built a solution, recruited volunteers, and earned recognition from multiple institutions, all before finishing high school.Qian’s work is ongoing. ReTech for Kids continues to collect, refurbish, and distribute devices, and the organisation is developing ReTechOS to make its devices even more accessible to first-time computer users.The combination of a $5,000 prize, a Diana Award, and a growing volunteer network suggests the initiative has momentum. What began as a student-led effort to close a gap has become a model that could expand further, reaching more students and diverting more devices from landfills.For Qian, the goal is simple. Technology should not be a barrier to learning, and a device that still works should not end up in a landfill when it could help a student build a future.
Article Summary: Chris Qian founded ReTech for Kids, a nonprofit that collects, refurbishes, and redistributes second-hand technology to under-resourced students. The initiative has mobilised more than 100 youth volunteers, helped distribute 2,000 refurbished devices, and earned Qian a $5,000 prize at the University of Vermont’s 2026 Vermont Pitch Challenge.

Article Title: Nominee vs legal heir: What is the difference and who has claim on assets? All you need to know
Article Text:
AI image

Who is a Nominee?



Who is a Legal Heir?

Difference between a Nominee and a Legal heir

Aspect Nominee Legal Heir Role Custodian Owner Transfer of Assets Can be done without any legal formalities. Requires testamentary documents for proof of ownership. Powers No power to transact, use, or transfer assets. Power to use and transact assets as an owner. Appointment Owner can appoint anyone, but some institutions specify certain conditions. Determined by succession/personal laws. Legal Right Cannot contest ownership legally. Can contest ownership in a court of law.

When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.
Article Summary: A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets. The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away. To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will.

Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.

Article Title: How to get your CIBIL credit score without a PAN card
Article Text:
Your credit score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity.

What is a CIBIL score?

How to get your CIBIL Credit score without a PAN Card

Factors affecting your CIBIL score

CIBIL credit score : Understanding your creditworthiness is pivotal in today's financial landscape, especially when seeking loans or credit cards. The Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited, commonly known as CIBIL, plays an important role in this regard by providing credit scores to borrowers.According to ET, credit score helps banks make informed decisions about extending credit cards and loans. Your credit history influences your CIBIL score , which is calculated using a special method.Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.1. Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. If you don’t have a PAN Card, you can use an alternative identification such as Passport, Voter ID, Driver’s License, or Ration Card. Enter the number of the chosen ID.3. Provide your date of birth, PIN code, and select your state. Finally, enter your mobile number and click on ‘Accept and Continue’.4. Authenticate your identity by entering the OTP (One-Time Password) delivered to your mobile device on the next screen. Click 'Continue' to proceed.5. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Upon successful registration, you will see a page confirming that 'You have successfully registered!'7. Click on ‘Go to Dashboard’ to access and view your CIBIL score.The factors influencing the new CIBIL score, as stated on the CIBIL website, include:1. Depth of credit: This refers to the duration of your existing credit history, calculated from the opening date of your oldest credit account.2. Long-term trend of outstanding balances: The overall trend of outstanding balances over time affects your score.3. Transaction history on credit cards: How you manage transactions on your credit cards impacts your score.4. Ratio of actual repayment amount to total amount due: This ratio indicates your repayment behavior and influences your score accordingly.5. Number of new accounts opened and number of accounts closed: Opening or closing accounts can affect your score, so managing these actions wisely is important.

Article Title: Instagram tests 90-minute horizontal videos - what it means for long-form content creators
Article Text:

Instagram on Monday began testing new features, including 90-minute horizontal videos to target long-form content creators like podcasters and comedians, with select creators in the US.The feature, called “Features”, will allow them to link short reel clips, typically around three minutes or less, to full-length videos, as per The Hollywood Reporter.“What you’re now going to be able to do is, you see a clip of a podcast that you love, you can just click and continue watching or watch the full video, and you’ll be able to dive in and see the whole thing because creators are going to be able to link these Reels to their overall feature,” vice-president of product at Instagram, Tessa Lyons, said.Instagram has already been testing Features with creators in Brazil and plans to expand the trial to tens of thousands of creators in the US. The videos will reportedly be recommended to users through the Explore page and other areas of the platform.The feature will be available on mobile, with Instagram aiming to extend the viewing experience to its TV app. Instagram for TV, which launched last year and is available on Samsung , Fire TV and Google TV, is now expanding to Apple TV in the US.“We think the best viewing experience for longform horizontal content is on a big, horizontal screen, and so I think that is where we will expect a lot of the deep consumption to happen over time,” Lyons said, as per The Hollywood Reporter.Instagram is also experimenting with “Series”, a feature that gives episodic Reels a dedicated space on a creator’s profile. The move comes amid growing interest in microdramas and episodic videos among creators.In June, the company began reaching out to microdrama studios in Southeast Asia to test the feature. It has since approached individual creators who have been experimenting with episodic content.Instagram plans to begin testing Series in more countries in the coming months, with a US launch targeted for the end of this year or early next year. The company has also started testing how the feature will appear on television.Other experiments include integrating live videos into the Reels tab and recommending them to users who do not follow the creators. The test is launching in Indonesia and Brazil, with an expansion to the US planned for next year.

Apple Intelligence features beyond Siri AI

Siri AI usage limits and what Apple plans to charge

Siri on the Mac has always been the version people forget is there, tucked into a menu bar icon most users click once and never again. The rebuilt assistant that arrived with macOS 27 Golden Gate on September 14 goes after that problem from a different angle, by putting itself inside Spotlight, inside the Control-click menu and behind a screenshot shortcut. The fastest way to reach Siri AI on a desktop now involves no talking at all.Mac owners also got a break nobody else did. Apple has withheld Siri AI from iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch across the European Union, yet Macs are carved out of that restriction. An EU account on macOS 27 Golden Gate can run the assistant provided the system language and Siri language are both English. Accounts registered in mainland China remain locked out on every device Apple sells.Switching it on is quick, but finishing the setup does not mean you can use it yet:The last of those puts you on a waitlist and the download begins on its own once you clear it. Apple gives no estimate for the wait, and reports since launch have swung between a few minutes and most of an afternoon. Running Apple Intelligence before you upgraded buys you nothing here, because that earlier consent does not carry over.Two lines cover eligibility. The A18 Pro MacBook Neo qualifies, and so does any Mac running M1 or newer.Intel machines are out, with no beta workaround.Underneath that sits a narrower requirement most people miss. Expressive voices, the setting that lets you dial Siri's pace and expressiveness, needs AFM Core Advanced, Apple's newest on-device model. On the Mac that translates to an M3 chip or later with at least 12GB of unified memory. An M1 MacBook Air will run the assistant fine and never see those controls.Language is the other limit. English is all Siri AI speaks for now, with French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish due next month, and both your system language and Siri language have to match a supported option.Most of the Mac-specific engineering has gone into access points rather than fresh abilities:Driving all of this is a new generation of Apple Foundation Models that the company says was built with Google, using its Gemini models. Requests are split between the Mac and Private Cloud Compute, where Apple's stated position is that personal data is never retained and stays out of reach of its own staff.Photos adds Spatial Reframing, an Extend tool and a rebuilt Clean Up. Image Playground handles photorealistic output now and accepts edits by description, with SynthID watermarking due in a later release. Safari sorts tabs into topics by itself, tracks pages for restocks or price cuts through Notify Me, and assembles custom extensions from a written brief. Shortcuts takes the same route to automations, and Calendar accepts plain-language changes to events.Anything routed through Apple's servers, Siri AI included, draws on a daily allowance. The company has declined to publish a number, saying the ceiling moves with the feature, the complexity of the request and how loaded the system is at the time.What Apple has committed to is charging for expanded access at some point. There is no price, no date, and no indication of whether the current free allowance survives once that tier exists.

The rebuilt assistant that arrived with macOS 27 Golden Gate on September 14 goes after that problem from a different angle, by putting itself inside Spotlight, inside the Control- click menu and behind a screenshot shortcut. The fastest way to reach Siri AI on a desktop now involves no talking at all.

Article Title: How Bees helped engineers solve what has been regarded as Solar panels’ biggest flaw since invention; and has been a major waste of energy
Article Text:
Representative image

Why angled sunlight creates a problem for solar panels

How honeycomb geometry gives light another chance

Why engineers turned to the structure of a beehive

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Bees have inspired engineers to rethink solar panel design. The honeycomb structure behind their hives has provided a blueprint for tackling a persistent problem: sunlight reflecting away from panels instead of generating electricity. Conventional flat panels receive sunlight more directly around midday, but the sun's changing angle affects how much light they capture.Engineers have developed a concave, three-dimensional design that redirects reflected light towards another surface, giving it a second chance to be absorbed. According to a report by The Pulse, the honeycomb-inspired structure increased maximum power output by 142.3% compared with a flat panel under the same conditions, offering a way to reduce wasted sunlight without tracking motors.Traditional solar panels have a flat surface. As the sun moves across the sky, its rays strike that surface at different angles. When sunlight arrives at an oblique angle, reflection from the protective glass becomes a problem. Light that bounces away cannot contribute to the panel’s electricity output.The honeycomb-inspired design changes the path of that reflected light. Rather than relying on a single flat surface, it uses sloping surfaces arranged into concave structures.Inside the three-dimensional module, sunlight can strike one slanted wall and bounce towards the opposite wall. Instead of immediately escaping, the reflected light encounters another surface where it can be absorbed. This process, described as enhanced light recapture, is central to the design.The supplied material reports a maximum power output increase of 142.3% over a conventional flat panel. At a zero-degree angle, when sunlight strikes directly, output increased by 36.4%. At 60 degrees, the reported improvement was 61.8%.These figures describe increases in power output under the stated comparison conditions, rather than the proportion of sunlight converted into electricity.Honeycomb combines closely packed hexagonal cells with strength and efficient material use. Engineers used this natural geometry as the basis for their solar module.Tilting the walls creates small valleys that help retain light within the structure. The benefit comes from how those surfaces redirect sunlight, allowing neighbouring surfaces to capture photons that might otherwise escape.To support the arrangement, engineers developed a flexible, printed polymer mechanical metamaterial, which is a structure whose engineered pattern helps determine its mechanical behaviour.The flexible backing could extend the design beyond flat rooftops. The report identifies curved walls, electric vehicles and aerospace equipment as potential applications.Its ability to fit curved surfaces could allow solar modules to be incorporated into places where conventional flat panels are difficult to install.
Article Summary: Engineers have developed a concave, three-dimensional design that redirects reflected light towards another surface, giving it a second chance to be absorbed. The honeycomb-inspired structure increased maximum power output by 142.3% compared with a flat panel under the same conditions.

Article Title: Meta fined $887 million for accessing Android users' photos; Italian regulator cites 'lack of co-operation'; gives 60-day deadline to disable the feature
Article Text:
Italy's data watchdog penalises Meta over alleged unauthorised access to Android users' personal photos and videos

Meta gets 60-day deadline

Meta ordered to pay $25 billion penalty to New Mexico

Facebook and Instagram parent Meta has been fined in Italy. Italian regulators have fined the social media giant Meta $887 million for accessing Android smartphone users' photos and videos without their specific consent. The Italian regulator said that the company had accessed Android users' photographs and videos without obtaining their consent or informing them. The fine is among the largest an Italian authority has ever imposed on a technology company.Italy's Data Protection Authority said that Meta did not properly inform about 20 million smartphone users that it had access to their photos and videos via a feature of the Facebook app.In its order, the regulator has given Meta 60 days to disable the feature by default and seek users' consent separately for access.The charge is related to a feature which suggests photos and videos from a user's phone gallery as ideas for posts. Facebook requested access to users' photo galleries through a single app-wide authorisation. According to the Italian regulator, a preceding notice did not make clear that this would also allow Facebook to generate suggestions based on photos in users' phone gallery.The regulator said that it took into account "the high number of people affected" and the fact it is "still ongoing for those who have not updated the app and for those who have already given their consent to the system".It also cited "Meta's lack of co-operation". The investigation, ‌which ⁠began in 2025, did not cover the possible use of the content to train artificial intelligence models, a practice Meta denied, ​the authority ​said. It added ⁠that it reserved the right to assess separately a new ​feature, launched in 2026, that allows ​content ⁠from users' galleries to be processed in the cloudIn October, Meta was hit with its largest fine ever for its business practices. A US judge in New Mexico ordered the company to pay $25 billion after it found that it had spent years lying to the public about how it handled Facebook user data.The ruling came in ‌a case related to allegations that Cambridge Analytica, a British political consulting company involved in Donald Trump's 2016 presidential campaign, obtained data from millions of Facebook users without their consent. New Mexico had sued Meta, accusing it of lying to Facebook users in New Mexico about who had access to their data. "Facebook's wrongdoing — over the course of years and systematically broadcast to the public — goes to the heart of Facebook's core business practices," Judge ​Francis Mathew wrote in his order, which came more than three weeks after the verdict.
Article Summary: Italy's Data Protection Authority said that Meta did not properly inform about 20 million smartphone users that it had access to their photos and videos. The fine is among the largest an Italian authority has ever imposed on a technology company. The regulator has given Meta 60 days to disable the feature by default and seek users' consent separately.

Article Title: Microsoft has an 'email warning' for its Outlook and Teams users after 24-hour-plus outage; says: Do not …
Article Text:
Microsoft has an 'email warning' for its Outlook and Teams users after 24-hour-plus outage; says: Do not …

Here’s what Microsoft said

Microsoft has issued an email warning for Outlook and Teams users following a 24-hour-plus Microsoft 365 service disruption on November 12. In an X (formerly Twitter) post, the company said that cybercriminals are exploiting the outage to send phishing emails that impersonate official service health notifications. Some messages claim that emails held during the disruption will be deleted within 24 hours unless users click a link to restore them. Microsoft has urged organisations to verify service alerts through the Microsoft 365 admin centre and investigate suspicious emails. "Microsoft Threat Intelligence observed an active phishing campaign exploiting the Microsoft 365 service disruption on November 12. The messages impersonate Microsoft 365 service health notifications and reference the legitimate Exchange Online incident EX1550543," the post said."Organizations should verify their Safe Links policies, investigate potential user interactions, and confirm service disruptions directly through the Microsoft 365 admin center,” it stated.In the X post, Microsoft Threat Intelligence wrote:“Microsoft Threat Intelligence observed an active phishing campaign exploiting the Microsoft 365 service disruption on November 12. The messages impersonate Microsoft 365 service health notifications and reference the legitimate Exchange Online incident EX1550543.Some of the phishing emails Microsoft detected on November 13 falsely claim that messages were held during the outage and will be deleted within 24 hours unless recipients click to restore them.Observed subjects follow the pattern "Outage - [six-character code]," with sender display names using organization-specific prefixes followed by "Outage Notification" or "Service Health."The campaign uses three sender domains, moments-notice[.]com, planetmaison[.]com, and newbooker[.]com, with recipient-specific SendGrid click-tracking links redirecting to reallifeaccounting[.]com, including the observed path /themelist0.html. Similar messages targeted organizations across multiple US sectors.The activity is consistent with credential phishing, although credential collection and malware delivery have not been confirmed.Security teams can use Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Threat Explorer and Microsoft Defender XDR advanced hunting (EmailEvents, EmailUrlInfo, and UrlClickEvents) to identify suspicious messages, examine embedded URLs, and investigate user clicks.Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Safe Links provides time-of-click protection against malicious URLs when properly configured. Organizations should verify their Safe Links policies, investigate potential user interactions, and confirm service disruptions directly through the Microsoft 365 admin center.”

Some messages claim that emails held during the disruption will be deleted within 24 hours unless users click a link to restore them.

Article Title: CUPRA unveils sporty Raval, new Formula E car at Paris Motor Show
Article Text:
Cupra Kiro new car

CUPRA Raval gets a sporty new look

Raval orders cross 50,000 as CUPRA targets further growth

CUPRA KIRO reveals new Formula E car for 2026/27

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

CUPRA has showcased several new products and technologies at the Paris Motor Show. The highlights include a new styling package for its Raval electric hatchback, a new Formula E car for the 2026/27 season and an updated audio system developed with Sennheiser. The company also displayed the Tindaya show car, which offers a glimpse of its future design plans. The exhibits are on display in Pavilion 4 from October 12 to 18.CUPRA has introduced the CUSTOM CUPRA by ABT package for its Raval electric hatchback. The package was previously available for the Leon and Formentor models.Inspired by the UrbanRebel concept, the new package adds front and rear splitters, side skirts, a large roof spoiler and winglets. It also includes 19-inch Sport Black Matt alloy wheels, ABT lettering, Dark Chrome CUPRA logos and special interior details.ID@undefined Caption not available.The package focuses on design, and CUPRA has not announced any changes to the car's performance. Customers will be able to select the package for certain Raval variants through the company's online configurator from the end of November 2026.For new cars, the parts will be handcrafted at the CUPRA Racing Factory before being fitted.Existing Raval owners can also get the package installed later through authorised dealers.The Raval is an important model for CUPRA as the company expands its electric vehicle range. The car is produced at the Martorell plant in Spain, where SEAT and CUPRA have invested more than €3 billion in electric vehicle production.The factory also plays a key role in the Volkswagen Group's Electric Urban Car Family, which includes four electric models from CUPRA, Volkswagen and Škoda.CUPRA said it had received more than 50,000 orders for the Raval since April, more than twice its original forecast. Nearly 15,000 cars have been delivered so far.The brand's sales chief, Sven Schuwirth, said CUPRA aims to sell 100,000 Raval units next year. If it reaches that target, the electric hatchback will become the company's best-selling model.CUPRA also reported more than 250,000 deliveries between January and September, an increase of 2% compared with the same period last year.Demand for battery-electric vehicles (BEVs) grew much faster. Orders for these models increased by 79% to more than 108,000. Nearly half of all orders received in the third quarter were for fully electric vehicles.The planned features include an illuminated logo, indicators that project onto the ground and a top speed of up to 190 km/h. The car will also get a reversing assist feature that can retrace up to 50 metres of its previous forward path.CUPRA also presented its new Formula E car for the 2026/27 season. The car, powered by Porsche technology, marks the team's entry into the championship's GEN4 era. The new generation of Formula E cars can reach speeds of more than 335 km/h and accelerate from 0 to 100 km/h in less than two seconds. They also feature permanent all-wheel drive.The car retains the team's signature copper colour scheme.ID@undefined Caption not available.British driver Jake Hughes will join the team for the new season. He brings experience from Formula E, including two podium finishes and four pole positions.Pepe Martí will continue for a second season. He was the highest-placed rookie in the previous season and secured podium finishes in Monaco and Sanya.CUPRA also used the event to showcase new in-car audio technology. The Tavascan Black Edition features the SENNHEISER AMBEO Immersive Sound System. Four actuators positioned along the roofline add a height effect to create a 360-degree audio experience. The updated Formentor and Terramar models will also receive the same system. Meanwhile, the Leon and Leon Sportstourer will offer the IMMERSIVE BY SENNHEISER audio system.Also read: Taylor Barnard joins Fortescue Zero Racing for Formula E's GEN4 era in 2026/27
Article Summary: CUPRA has unveiled a new styling package for its Raval electric hatchback. The company also presented its new Formula E car for the 2026/27 season. CUPRA also used the event to showcase new in-car audio technology.

Article Title: Jaguar unveils Type 01 electric car with 1,030PS power and 450-mile range
Article Text:
Jaguar Type 01

Jaguar Type 01 revealed: 0-62mph in 3.2 seconds, 450-mile range and luxury cabin

A modern cabin with new technology

What does the Type 01 name mean?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

When will the Jaguar Type 01 go on sale?

Jaguar on Friday unveiled the Type 01, an all-electric luxury car that marks a new beginning for the British carmaker. Revealed in New York City, the four-door grand tourer combines high performance with modern design and new technology. One of the car's biggest highlights is its acceleration. It can go from 0 to 62 mph in just 3.2 seconds. It has three electric motors that produce 1,030PS of power and 1,365Nm of torque.The Type 01 is Jaguar's new flagship electric car. It comes with a 118kWh usable battery pack and offers a claimed range of up to 400 miles under US EPA testing. Its range is up to 450 miles (720km) under WLTP testing.The car uses an 850-volt electrical system that supports fast charging. When connected to a 350kW DC fast charger, it can add 200 miles of range in just 13 minutes.ID@undefined Caption not available.Built on Jaguar's new Electric Architecture (JEA), the Type 01 has been designed to offer a balance of performance and comfort. Its design includes a low roof, a long bonnet, a short front overhang and large 23-inch wheels. The car also has a 50:50 weight distribution, which is aimed at improving handling.Jaguar has also added intelligent torque vectoring and active aerodynamics to improve performance. These features include movable air vents and a rear spoiler that can extend in three stages. The car has a drag coefficient of 0.23, helping it move through the air more efficiently.The Type 01 has a cabin designed around luxury and technology. A central section divides the interior into four separate areas.The cabin features brass-effect aluminium trim, a 24-inch OLED driver display made from a single piece of glass and a separate 7-inch touchscreen. It also gets a full-width panoramic soundbar and seats with audio features designed to improve the listening experience.Jaguar says the name Type 01 reflects both its history and its future. The word "Type" pays tribute to famous models from the brand's past. The number "0" represents zero emissions, while "1" marks the first car of its new generation.The car also benefits from technology developed through Jaguar TCS Racing's Formula E programme, which has won two world championships.The Type 01 can accelerate from 62 mph to 112 mph (100km/h to 180km/h) in just 4.0 seconds.Designed, engineered and manufactured in the UK, the Type 01 is an important part of Jaguar's move towards becoming a fully electric luxury car brand. Prices start at £130,000, with the US price listed at $130,500. Higher-specification versions and customised models are expected to cost more than £150,000.Jaguar plans to open order books in early 2027, with the first customer deliveries expected in the second half of the year.Also read: Sebastien Buemi ends full-time Formula E career, stays with Envision as advisor
Article Summary: The Type 01 is Jaguar's new flagship electric car. It has three electric motors that produce 1,030PS of power and 1,365Nm of torque. It can go from 0 to 62 mph in just 3.2 seconds. Prices start at £130,000, with the US price listed at $130,500.

Article Title: Formula E names COMSOL its Official Multiphysics Partner in new multi-year deal
Article Text:
Formula E and Comsol

Formula E joins hands with COMSOL to boost electric racing technology

AI and digital twins also in focus

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

GEN4 to bring bigger technology demands

Formula E on Thursday announced a new multi-year partnership with COMSOL, which will become the Official Multiphysics Partner of the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship. The partnership brings together Formula E, the world's leading all-electric motorsport championship, and COMSOL, a company known for its multiphysics simulation and computer-aided engineering software. As part of the partnership, Formula E and COMSOL engineers will use COMSOL Multiphysics to study complex engineering problems involving several physical systems working together.Electric race cars depend on several systems at the same time. These include electrical, thermal, structural, electromagnetic, fluid and battery systems.All these systems have to work together under tough performance and energy limits. COMSOL will provide Formula E's technology teams with simulation software and technical expertise to help them understand how these different physical effects interact.ID@undefined Caption not available.The partnership will also look at simulation apps and digital twin technology. The aim is to make engineering information easier to use outside the traditional modelling process.Bjorn Sjodin, SVP of Product Management at COMSOL, said, “Formula E is a great example of why multiphysics simulation matters, as multiple phenomena are at play and constantly interact with one another.We are excited to work directly with Formula E's technology team and put COMSOL Multiphysics to work on these kinds of real-world challenges.”Formula E CTO Dan Cherowbrier said the partnership will strengthen the championship's engineering capabilities.“Technology is at the heart of Formula E, so partnering with COMSOL makes real sense for us and truly enhances our engineering skillsets. COMSOL gives us a powerful environment for understanding complex systems where many different physical effects are connected, but the opportunity goes beyond individual simulations. We're particularly interested in how AI-assisted modelling, agentic workflows, and digital twins can help engineers interact with models, explore designs, and make simulation insight more accessible as we continue to push the limits of electric racing,” he said.The partnership comes as Formula E prepares for the next generation of its cars.The GEN4 era will bring greater demands in areas such as speed, efficiency, energy management and vehicle development. It will introduce what Formula E describes as its fastest and most technologically advanced race car so far.COMSOL has also announced COMSOL Multiphysics version 2027, which is scheduled to arrive later this autumn.The new version will include features aimed at advanced engineering work, including dedicated electric motor modelling, system-level simulation, agentic modelling and wider access to tools for creating simulation apps.The partnership was announced at the COMSOL Conference 2026 Boston. Formula E CTO Dan Cherowbrier also delivered a keynote speech at the event, discussing the technology and engineering that could shape the future of Formula E.
Article Summary: Formula E joins hands with COMSOL to boost electric racing technology. Aim is to make engineering information easier to use outside the traditional modelling process. AI and digital twins also in focus as Formula E prepares for the next generation of its cars.
